newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. oil-for-food deal fails to help Iraqis - paper.
newsitem.headline: U.N. oil-for-food deal fails to help Iraqis - paper.

text.p: Iraq's ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra said on Monday a United Nations oil-for-food deal had failed to ease the hardships of the Iraqi people living under U.N. sanctions.
In a front-page editorial the paper blamed the United States for the sluggish implementation of the pact, accusing Washington of tryng to disrupt the deal.
"After one year of signing the memorandum and more than five months of its application...the Iraqi people are still suffering," Thawra said in a front-page editorial.
"America is still creating excuses and obstacles to impede its (the deal) implementation," it said, adding "it (U.S.) wants the Iraqi people to stay poor and live under its manoeuvres and decisions."

The deal, which was signed on May 20 last year and went into effect last December, allows Iraq to export $2 billion worth of oil to buy urgently needed goods for Iraqis, suffering from U.N. sanctions imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Food supplies purchased by the oil money are piling up in Iraq and the first shipment of medicine arrived this month.
Thawra said the United States' representative at the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq was delaying the approval of food and medicine contracts under the pact.
It said Iraq had submitted a total of 556 contracts with foreign firms but only 169 of them went through.

United Nations officials in Baghdad said on Sunday the current Turkish incursion in northern Iraq might block implemetation of the deal and destablise northern Iraq, out of the control of the central government since the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
